title: What is evangelism? Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of him to every town and place where he was about to go. He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into his harvest field. Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves. Do not take a purse or bag or sandals; and do not greet anyone on the road. When you enter a house, first say, ‘Peace to this house. If someone who promotes peace is there, your peace will rest on them; if not, it will return to you. Stay there, eating and drinking whatever they give you, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move around from house to house. “When you enter a town and are welcomed, eat what is offered to you. Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’ But when you enter a town and are not welcomed, go into its streets and say, ‘Even the dust of your town we wipe from our feet as a warning to you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God has come near.’ I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town. “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you. And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted to the heavens? No, you will go down to Hades. “Whoever listens to you listens to me; whoever rejects you rejects me; but whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
devotional:
The peace of evangelism.

Jesus goes on to say: ‘When you enter a house, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’ If someone who promotes peace is there, your peace will rest on them; if not, it will return to you. Stay there, eating and drinking whatever they give you, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move around from house to house.’

This is one of those passages we could easily skip over and miss some important principles. Jesus instructs us ‘First say ‘peace to this house.’ This may feel a bit counter intuitive, because we may think that we are there to share the gospel or share what Jesus has done for us. But before we do that we need to communicate that the God we love and serve wants to bless that person and their home with his peace.

People need to know about our peace, love and acceptance of them before they can receive the gospel. Evangelism is not just giving people an opportunity to share in the life of Jesus, it is also an opportunity to share in our lives. Look carefully at what Jesus said. ‘If someone who promotes peace is there, your peace will rest on them;’ He did not speak about ‘his’ peace or ‘my’ peace but your peace. In other words, the heart condition of the person doing the evangelism is the most important and essential factor in evangelism. The peace we experience is because of our theology, [what we believe and know about God,] and not our circumstances.

If we share the gospel in such a way that causes someone to feel threatened or intimated by our conduct then we have lost the right to share Jesus with them. Charles Blow, wrote, “One doesn’t have to operate with great malice to do great harm. The absence of empathy and understanding are sufficient.”

It is possible to be vulnerable like ‘lambs among wolves,’ and have a deep sense of the peace of God at the same time. These two emotional experiences need not be mutually exclusive. Peace is a settled confidence that although you are as vulnerable as lambs among wolves, you are sure that God is in control. This is the only secure base we can evangelise from.

The conduct of the evangelist

We need to hold lightly to our religious traditions. Look at what Jesus said, ‘Stay there, eating and drinking whatever they give you,’

This was quite a radical thing to say to young Jews, who would only have eaten ritually clean food. Because the mission they were being sent on was to the other side of the Jordan, which was a Gentile region, and if they accepted hospitality, they would have to eat unclean food. So Jesus is saying that, in order to be successful in their mission, they would have to hold lightly to their religiosity and their rituals, and immerse themselves in the local culture so that there would be no barriers for others to receive Christ.

We need to assure people know that God cares for all of their lives.

Jesus said, ‘Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’ People need to know that they are more than souls who need to be saved. When we are in conversation with someone and they are not well, we should offer to pray for them. It may be God’s will to heal them, but you wont know until you try.

How we respond to the rejection of the gospel is part of our evangelism.

Doing evangelism the way Jesus instructed does not guarantee results, but it does guarantee faithfulness.

‘Look at what Jesus said, ‘But when you enter a town and are not welcomed, go into its streets and say, ‘Even the dust of your town we wipe from our feet as a warning to you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God has come near.’ I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.’

This verse raises an important issue that we need to think through. Is the critique of someone’s response to our evangelism, [be it a positive or negative response,] to be part of our evangelism. I find this very challenging because all my life when I have received a negative reaction to evangelism, my natural response has been to thank the person for their time and politely leave, which has seemed like an appropriate response. Not according to Jesus.

If we are shown rejection because we have shared the gospel, it is okay to share our sadness. Showing our sadness is important because it shows that we really care. I remember a long time ago someone came to our door and tried to sell us a vacuum cleaner. We refused to buy one. The man left, probably frustrated but not upset because it was not a matter of life and death. Rejecting the gospel is a matter of life and death and that rejection should affect us, we are not door to door salesmen.

We need to find culturally appropriate ways of expressing our sadness without condemning or criticising others. Expressing our sadness is an evidence that we really care. Sharing our sadness of a persons refusal to accept the gospel should be part of our evangelism.

Shaking of the dust of rejection.

Rejection is a terrible and painful thing that can prevent us from moving forward. Don’t pretend it is OK to be rejected, it isn’t, don’t play it down, don’t over spiritualise it, nor should you sit there pleading your case trying to make them want you, or conforming to someone you’re not, shake the dust off your feet and keep moving!

So much of our pain comes from trying to change the way others feel about us. Shaking dust off of one’s feet was not an act of rejection, but an act of warning. You shouldn’t respond to rejection with rejection, nor should you fight fire with more fire. This was a sign of deep concern with the direction one’s own community was headed in. It was an expression of anxiety not judgement.

I wonder do we care enough to demonstrate our sadness when people reject the gospel. Or are we more like sales men?

Bible reading in a year plan: - Hosea 5-8.
prayer: Father, please help me have a Godly character so I can share the gospel with others.
